paragraphs: Rav Sheila, in Rav's and Shmuel's time. He permitted marriage in a case of waters with no visible end. Yevamot 121a: a man drowned in the Agam of Samkei, and Rav Sheila permitted his wife to marry. Rav told Shmuel, ‘Let us excommunicate him.’ He replied, ‘Let us first send to him.’ They sent: ‘In waters with no visible end, is his wife forbidden or permitted?’ He sent back, ‘Forbidden.’ ‘Is the Agam of Samkei water with an end or without an end?’ He answered, ‘Without an end.’ ‘Why, then, did the master act this way?’ ‘I made a mistake,’ etc. Shmuel applied to Rav, ‘No wrong shall befall the righteous,’ and Rav applied to Shmuel, ‘Salvation is in much counsel,’ etc. He headed a study session in Babylonia, and Rav stood over him as public expounder (see there). Rav Hisda said that R' Sheila said: Berakhot 15b; Ketubbot 75a. Rav Nahman said that Rav Sheila said that Rav said: Berakhot 49, beginning of b. Those of R' Sheila's school say: Rosh Hashanah 23a; Ta'anit 11a. Rav Adda reported a teaching of R' Sheila’s school in Sanhedrin 108b. In Sanhedrin 109a, they laughed in the West at a different teaching from the same school. I do not know whether this Rav Sheila is different from the one mentioned before, but Yuhasin divided them into two. The judge is also called R' Sheila, and this one Rav Sheila. I am also uncertain whose son Rabbah bar Sheila was; they call him Rabbah bar Sheila, not bar Rav or bar R' Sheila.
